generated_from: HDR-mechanistic pipeline v3.5 + R6 reconciliation + tau/timescale reconciliation

timescale_architecture.description: Two-timescale decomposition of the 9-axis system. Fast axes participate in perturbation-recovery dynamics (OU model). Quasi-static axes drift secularly and modulate fast-axis couplings but do not recover from perturbation on intervention timescales.

B.note: tau_B = 90-120d. Quasi-static for interventions < 6 months; dynamical for longer horizons. Include in the dynamical subsystem for 1-2 year simulations; exclude for < 6 month.

timescale_architecture.rationale: The spectral abscissa alpha(A) governs perturbation-recovery dynamics. Only axes that actually recover from perturbation should contribute to alpha. Axes with tau >> simulation horizon drift secularly and should be treated as slowly varying parameters, not dynamical state variables. This is standard singular perturbation theory applied to the HDR OU model.

I.evidence: CRP half-life 19h (acute phase); full inflammatory resolution 7-25 days depending on stimulus. Young healthy: ~7d. Older/chronic: ~25d.
I.previous_interpretation: CRP half-life only (acute phase protein, not full resolution)

M.evidence: Postprandial glucose excursion resolves in 2-4 hours in healthy individuals. HOMA-IR is a steady-state measure, not a perturbation-recovery measure. The OU τ_M should reflect the speed of glucose homeostasis, not HOMA-IR recovery.
M.previous_interpretation: HOMA-IR recovery post-illness (capacity rebuilding, not perturbation recovery)

E.evidence: Epigenetic modifications are quasi-permanent. The 'recovery' timescale is the rate of passive demethylation/remethylation, which is very slow (years). The DunedinPACE inter-assay interval (180d) measures assessment frequency, not biological recovery. The R6 value (~1000d) better captures the actual drift timescale.
E.age_dependence: minimal — epigenetic drift is quasi-irreversible on intervention timescales
E.previous_interpretation: DunedinPACE inter-assay interval (measurement frequency, not biology)

mito.evidence: NAD+/NADH ratio recovers from metabolic stress within hours to days. Mitochondrial membrane potential recovery is hours. mtDNA copy number turnover (30 days) is a compensatory response, not the perturbation timescale. The OU τ should capture acute bioenergetic recovery.
mito.previous_interpretation: mtDNA-CN turnover (compensatory marker, not acute recovery)

P.evidence: Proteasome half-life ~hours. Autophagosome formation and cargo clearance takes 1-2 days. Misfolded protein bolus cleared within days in healthy cells. The 7-day estimate was for proteostasis 'capacity' restoration, not single-perturbation clearance.
P.previous_interpretation: Proteostasis flux estimate (capacity measure, not perturbation recovery)

C.evidence: Circadian re-entrainment after phase shift takes 1-3 days (1 day per hour of shift is the clinical rule). The export value (1 day) is at the fast end; 2 days is a better central estimate.

N.evidence: The baroreflex operates on a beat-to-beat timescale (seconds), but the OU model axis N represents autonomic/HPA regulatory BALANCE, not the baroreflex itself. HPA axis recovery after acute stress takes hours; cortisol diurnal rhythm restoration after disruption takes 1-2 days. The 0.007-day (10-minute) value was confusing the baroreflex mechanism with the regulatory axis.
N.previous_interpretation: Baroreflex recovery (mechanism timescale, not axis regulatory timescale)

F.evidence: Grip strength recovery after immobilisation/deconditioning takes 2-6 weeks. Muscle protein synthesis rate recovers from acute exercise within 1-2 days, but the functional axis (grip, gait, SPPB) takes weeks. The R6 range (8-42d) is well-supported.
F.previous_interpretation: Muscle protein synthesis cycle (close but at slow end)

B.evidence: Bone remodelling cycle (BMU activation → resorption → formation → quiescence) takes 3-4 months. This is both the perturbation-recovery and capacity timescale for bone — they're the same because bone remodelling IS the recovery mechanism.
